test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (English) (Held on: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. There are several factors that contribute to wisdom.

B. Doing this has become more difficult than before owing to the complexity of the specialised knowledge required.

C. This is the capacity to take account of all important factors in a problem and to attach to each its due weight.

D. Of these, I should put first a sense of proportion.
solution:
The correct answer is '**ADCB**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
 
• **Sentence A **will be the first sentence because it introduces a sentence that tells us about wisdom.
 
• **Sentence D** will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence.
 
• **Sentence C **will be the next sentence.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence B** will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence:
 
 
• **A**: There are several factors that contribute to wisdom.​
 
• **D**: Of these, I should put first a sense of proportion.
 
• **C**: This is the capacity to take account of all important factors in a problem and to attach to each its due weight.
 
• **B**: Doing this has become more difficult than before owing to the complexity of the specialised knowledge required.

 
 
 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** *There are several factors that contribute to wisdom.​ Of these, I should put first a sense of proportion. This is the capacity to take account of all important factors in a problem and to attach to each its due weight. Doing this has become more difficult than before owing to the complexity of the specialised knowledge required.*
